questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or let someone else drive. Tiredness makes it hard to think and slows your reactions. This makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Look behind the vehicle before getting in.
Only use your mirrors.
Back up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind the vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Look behind the vehicle before getting in. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely and stay stopped until the signal arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Who do drivers turning left need to yield to?

options.text: Cars that are passing.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to cars driving straight ahead. You can only turn when it is safe and you will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with red flashing lights?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing. Do not move until the lights stop. If the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about the argument.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. If you are very angry, excited, afraid, worried, or sad, wait to calm down before driving. You need to focus your mind on driving without thinking about what upset you.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than regular cars.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to turn than regular cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than regular cars traveling at the same speed. A regular car at 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait for the truck or bus to turn first.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to turn first.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus is stopped on the road to load or unload children?

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: Stop completely and wait until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back. Even after the bus starts moving, do not proceed until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you just passed before returning to your lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to move back to your lane.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
Drive slowly in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through a flooded road. Floodwater may hide dangers you cannot see. If you see a flooded area, turn around and use a different route.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Change lanes quickly and often.
Change lanes when a car is in your blind spot.
Change lanes slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Change lanes only when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: If you must stop on an interstate highway in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to get the attention of passing cars.
Get out of your car and wave down the first passing vehicle.
Pull onto the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull onto the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of high-speed traffic.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Watch for posted speed limits and watch the road carefully. Workers may be present.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Adjust your speed to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop completely behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates are raised.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates are raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning lights, or flaggers tell you a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of the darkness and glare from other headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave at least three to four seconds of distance between you and a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely, you risk hitting the rider if they fall. Wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks increase the chance of a fall.

questions.question: What should a driver do if pedestrians are in a crosswalk?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Turn right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the pedestrians have finished crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Allow enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do before driving after taking medicine?

options.text: Talk to your doctor about how it affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to your doctor about how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Medicines, both prescription and over-the-counter, can affect your driving ability. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine will affect you before you drive.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Use your brakes lightly only after the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a work zone?

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and don't tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and don't tailgate.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Don't tailgate and increase your following distance.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing and is in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go ahead because you have the right-of-way.
Go ahead if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let pedestrians in the intersection cross first. Wait until they have completely crossed before you go.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and lower your visibility.

questions.question: When is it okay to drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver won't expect you there and might pull off the road.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using white canes or guide dogs.

questions.question: How can you let other drivers know you are there at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you can't see clearly or when other drivers might not see you. Use low beams if your windshield wipers are on.
